chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from Muawiya bin Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The stingy is the one who is stingy with the peace (greeting).
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a stingy person in Shia hadith beyond just money?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq, compiling this in *Mani al-Akhbar*, elevates the greeting (*salam*) from a mere social nicety to a fundamental act of generosity (*karam*), reflecting the Shia emphasis on *silat al-rahib* (maintaining kinship ties) as a core religious duty. This definition aligns with the Prophetic tradition that stinginess is not just financial but includes withholding rights of companionship and peace, thereby framing social warmth as a spiritual currency.
